issues.legal_issue: Retrospective application of rules imposing special charges for unauthorized canal-water use does not violate the constitutional protection against retrospective punishment when the use is not an offence and the charges are not penalties.
material_facts: The appellants used canal water without authorization, and canal authorities assessed special charges for that use.
The authorities assessed the charges as payment for water used; they were not trying the appellants for an offence.
No law prohibited the unauthorized use of the water, although the applicable rules permitted special rates to be charged for it.
The rules were applied retrospectively, and the appellants challenged the resulting charges as a greater penalty than could have been imposed when the water was used.
issues.conclusion: The water use was not an offence, and the special rates were charges for water used rather than penalties for an offence. The retrospective application of the rules therefore did not attract the constitutional protection against retrospective punishment.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 20(1) of the Constitution, an offence means an act or omission made punishable by law, as provided by Section 3(37) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, applied through Article 367. As explained in Maqbool Hussain v. State of Bombay, [1953] SCR 730, the constitutional term is understood in that statutory sense. A charge for use of water under Section 31 of the Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, remains a charge rather than punishment where no law prohibits that use; its being imposed at special or high rates does not change its character. Rules 32 and 33 of the Sirhind Canal Rules provided for special rates, and Sections 3 and 4 of the Pepsu Sirhind Canal and Western Jumna Canal Rules (Enforcement and Validation) Act, 1954, applied and validated the rules retrospectively.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_retrospective_water_charge and no_law_prohibited_the_water_use and charge_was_for_water_used and authority_did_not_try_an_offence

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_retrospectiv: A person challenged the retrospective imposition of a charge for water use as a greater punishment than could have been imposed when the use occurred.
predicates.no_law_prohibited_the_water_use: No law forbade the person’s use of the water.
predicates.charge_was_for_water_used: An authority assessed a charge as payment for water the person had used.
predicates.authority_did_not_try_an_offence: The authority decided whether water had been used and what charge applied, rather than trying the person for an offence.

issues.definition: When a person challenges a retrospective water-use charge, and no law prohibited the use, the charge was payment for water used, and the authority did not try an offence, the charge is not a penalty for an offence.
